# Codex execution contract: production_plan

The owning Skill reads this file to constrain Codex inputs, decisions, and output. It is not a system prompt sent to an external text model. Braced fields are named input slots assembled from selected local project assets.

Execution role: short-drama production manager. Combine the director book, selected assets, selected storyboard, Provider capabilities, and user limits into a shot-level execution plan. Do not submit tasks.

[DIRECTOR BOOK]
{director_book}

[SELECTED STORYBOARD]
{storyboard}

[LOCAL ASSET LEDGER]
{asset_ledger}

[PROVIDER CAPABILITY CATALOG]
{provider_catalog}

[USER LIMITS AND CONFIRMED PARAMETERS]
{user_limits}

Return strict JSON only: {"episode_key":"...","source_versions":{},"shots":[...],"totals":{},"unresolved":[],"approved":false}.

Every shots item contains: shot_number, dependencies, storyboard_strategy, image_strategy, previz_strategy, video_strategy, audio_strategy, provider, model_or_workflow, prompt_profile, input_mode, duration_seconds, resolution, aspect_ratio, candidate_count, reference_assets, estimated_paid_calls, fallback, review_checks, status. storyboard_strategy.mode is exactly image or blender. image_strategy contains mode, board_type, panel_grid_size, and overflow_strategy. video_strategy always contains `visible_character_keys` and `visible_event_keys`. Only viral-recreation video_strategy contains depth_reference.

Rules:
1. Reference only local stable keys and selected versions that exist in the ledger. Put missing or wrong versions in unresolved.
2. Select only modalities and parameters declared by the Provider. Never invent a model, workflow, or cost.
3. Codex creates text prompts directly; do not plan an external text-model call.
4. totals summarizes task count by modality, material count, shot count, and total duration. Never calculate, guess, or display a price.
5. approved must be false when unresolved is non-empty, reference use is unconfirmed, the production plan is unconfirmed, or a required generation parameter is missing.
6. Initial status is exactly blocked or ready; never mark a shot ready with incomplete dependencies.
7. prompt_profile is exactly seedance2 or h3. Final generation uses character images, a temporal storyboard, a shot board, an audio reference, and the video prompt. Viral recreation additionally requires source-derived depth. A standard project adds Blender previz only when the two still boards cannot prove a complex route, multi-person interaction, exact contact, axis risk, or continuous camera move. Seedance 2.0 uses `full-reference`, and H3 uses `Ref2VA`. If the Provider cannot carry the inputs this shot actually requires, mark unresolved; never silently omit one.
8. When the Provider supports MiniMax H3 native audio (video.native-audio), default audio_strategy.mode to native and record a timed speech_timeline, one cross-shot music_anchor, and paired adjacent transition_pair values; do not schedule separate TTS for those shots. Use post-dub/independent only when the user explicitly requests dubbing or the Provider/model is confirmed to lack native audio; do not silently fall back to dubbing just because capability is unknown. Adjacent H3 transition_out and transition_in values must match as a pair.
9. Every shot uses image_strategy.mode=generate, board_type=shot-board, and panel_grid_size=2..16 (default 6, adjusted to actual beats), producing independent temporal-storyboard and shot-board assets. Standard projects default to storyboard_strategy.mode=image and previz_strategy={"mode":"none"}. Use storyboard_strategy.mode=blender with previz_strategy={"mode":"blender","purpose":"motion-reference","fps":12} only when the two boards still cannot unambiguously express a complex route, multi-person interaction, exact contact, axis risk, or continuous camera move; name that spatial risk in review_checks. Viral-recreation uses source depth and adds Blender review only when complex staging needs it. Only RunningHub minimax-h3-reference-to-video currently accepts the Blender motion reference; otherwise mark unresolved. Do not bind future asset versions. Composition elements require source, selected-asset, or confirmed-blocking evidence; block unsupported elements in unresolved. overflow_strategy is exactly compose-assets or reject.
10. Tailor review_checks to actual shot risk; every item must be a concrete, named, observable phrase (e.g. "mirror reflection consistency", "contact point readable through rain") derived from the contract's ai_risks and evidence elements: dialogue checks speaker identity and every visible mouth state; group shots check headcount, order, facing, and limb ownership; prop interaction checks before/contact/after states and adjacent objects; walking or fights check foot contact, weight, direction, speed, and pose across cuts; in-frame screens check whether precise post-production graphics are required. When composition risks apply, turn each into an explicit check: mirrors/glossy water verify the reflection matches the real person and actual dressing, with no extra fingers, camera, or reflection anomaly; rain, fog, neon, and smoke/dust verify the weather and colored light are evidenced, directions are consistent, and neither buries the contact point nor identity; crowd shots verify headcount, identity, costume-color anchors, and no extra bystanders; weapons and multi-hand interaction verify prop form, holding relationship, hand count, and before/contact/after states; a narrow door gap or foreground occlusion verifies visible width, both eyes intact, and the key action uncovered; high-speed trails verify both eyes, the face, and the contact point stay sharp and the subject is not a blob; front-and-back pincer/encirclement verifies both threats' identity, distance, and facing stay readable in foreground and background; vertical shots verify faces, key props, and contact points sit in the upper-middle safe area, the bottom subtitle safe area is clear, and motion edges keep a 10% margin. Keep only the risks this shot actually has. Never copy one generic checklist onto every shot.

11. Only a shot whose previz_strategy.mode is blender runs direct-blender-previz before generate-blender-previz renders and scores it. Previz never replaces the temporal storyboard, shot board, character, scene, prop, wardrobe, material, or final-look references.

12. Only viral-recreation writes video_strategy.depth_reference, using RunningHub workflow 2098674379113979905 and a selected per-shot clip cut from the original reference. Standard projects must not manufacture a source clip and convert it to depth; optional Blender previz becomes a `reference_video` only when the spatial-risk rule in item 9 applies. Depth and previz are mutually exclusive. Character images continue to own identity and appearance.

13. `video_strategy.visible_character_keys` lists every `char-*` that is actually visible in the shot and exactly matches the asset keys in storyboard `characters[].appearance`; an off-screen speaker is included only when visible. Every listed key binds one selected image in reference_assets with `role=character_identity`; never bind only the protagonist or speaker. Use an empty array for a shot with no visible character. `video_strategy.visible_event_keys` lists every stable visible event key that may produce action sound, or an empty array when none exists. Final video-prompts bind one temporal storyboard, one shot board, and one audio reference. Viral recreation additionally binds exactly one depth reference; standard shots bind exactly one Blender reference only when the plan enables it. An asset board is optional and never replaces either a character image or either storyboard.

14. Every native-audio ambience item carries `evidence:{source,detail}`, where source is script, storyboard, scene_asset, or audio_reference. Every action_sounds item carries an `evidence_event_key` that exactly references this shot's `visible_event_keys`. Never prescribe footsteps without a visible walking event, energy sound without a visible energy event, or generic "cinematic sound" without evidence.

No API key, token, remote business ID, Markdown, or explanation.
